evals.prompt: In this Obsidian vault, run /learn-quiz Processes in Learn/Operating Systems. Processes is Needs Validation. Ask one question at a time. My first answer will explain the concept independently and my second will apply it to a new failure scenario.
evals.expected_output: Creates an in-progress assessment before the first question, persists recall and transfer turns, derives a grounded strong outcome, then atomically marks Processes Mastered with Last Tested updated and appends exactly one linked history event.
assertions: The assessment artifact exists before the first question and has explicit lifecycle metadata and a fixed Processes topic set.
The skill asks one concise open-ended question at a time, persists the complete prompt before display, and records the source lesson heading for each question.
Each prompt has one core task, is answerable from its recorded lesson section, and does not bundle unrelated process, thread, context-switch, scheduling, and recovery concepts.
After each answer, the assistant visibly presents feedback and the correct answer or core model in chat rather than writing feedback only to Markdown.
Processes has independent recall and transfer evidence, verified grounding, and a strong topic outcome without copied lesson self-check wording.
Only Processes changes from Needs Validation to Mastered; Last Tested is today while Last Learned and Current Focus are preserved.
Exactly one append-only history event links the completed assessment, and the artifact ends with Status complete.

evals.prompt: Run /learn-quiz Threads in Learn/Operating Systems. Threads is Needs Validation. I will initially confuse process isolation with thread isolation, then correct myself after feedback.
evals.expected_output: Records the original misconception, gives immediate diagnostic feedback, permits one remediation follow-up, preserves the revised answer, caps the result at partial, and moves Threads to Needs Review.
assertions: Each Threads prompt is concise, has one core task, and records the exact lesson heading that grounds it.
The original answer remains in the assessment and the diagnosis identifies concept-confusion with the mistaken assumption and missing premise.
At most one remediation prompt is asked for Threads, and the revised answer plus follow-up feedback are persisted separately.
Successful remediation produces partial rather than strong.
Threads becomes Needs Review with Last Tested updated; Last Learned, Current Focus, and unrelated rows are preserved.
The completed assessment and exactly one linked history event summarize the misconception without duplicating the transcript.

evals.prompt: Run /learn-quiz Threads in Learn/Operating Systems. Threads is Needs Validation. For the recall question I will answer: I don't know. After feedback I will still be unable to explain the core concept.
evals.expected_output: Treats I don't know as a genuine knowledge gap, not a failed guess, uses one bounded follow-up, records weak evidence, and moves Threads to Needs Review.
assertions: The explicit non-answer is preserved and diagnosed as knowledge-gap rather than concept-confusion or an incorrect guess.
The skill provides focused feedback and no more than one remediation opportunity for the topic.
The unresolved core gap produces a weak topic outcome and Needs Review.
The quiz does not turn into a lesson, research new material, or invoke another skill.
Progress and history update only after the assessment is complete.

evals.prompt: Resume the in-progress Processes and Threads assessment in Learn/Operating Systems. Processes already has complete recall and transfer turns. Threads has a persisted unanswered transfer prompt. Continue without regenerating prior work.
evals.expected_output: Resumes the exact assessment and unanswered Threads prompt, preserves prior Processes evidence, and withholds all progress changes until both topics are complete before idempotent finalization.
assertions: The existing in-progress artifact is resumed instead of creating a new attempt.
Recorded Processes turns remain byte-preserved and the exact unanswered Threads prompt is displayed again.
No selected progress row changes while any selected topic lacks sufficient evidence.
After completion, both intended transitions are applied together and history contains exactly one assessment-linked event.
A resumed finalization does not duplicate progress effects or the history event.

evals.prompt: Run /learn-quiz Processes Threads in Learn/Operating Systems, then abandon it after the first Processes answer and start a fresh attempt with the same topics.
evals.expected_output: Preserves the partial attempt as abandoned without changing progress, then creates a distinct suffixed in-progress assessment with the same fixed topic set.
assertions: The first artifact is marked abandoned and its recorded prompt and answer are preserved.
Abandonment changes no progress row, date, Current Focus, or history.
The fresh attempt uses a distinct numeric-suffix filename rather than overwriting the first artifact.
The new artifact has Status in-progress and the confirmed immutable topic set.
No completion event is written for the abandoned attempt.

evals.prompt: Run /learn-quiz Context Switch in Learn/Operating Systems. The note is Needs Validation, but its explanation is explicitly unverified and does not trace to persisted resources. I will give excellent recall and transfer answers.
evals.expected_output: Assesses the eligible note but records unverified grounding, caps the otherwise strong evidence at partial, moves only the note to Needs Review, and leaves its source lesson unchanged.
assertions: An eligible notes/ progress row is accepted as the assessment unit.
The assessment records Grounding unverified because persisted workspace sources do not support its important claims.
The topic outcome is capped at partial and cannot produce Mastered despite excellent answers.
Only Context Switch becomes Needs Review with Last Tested updated; the source lesson's status is unchanged.
The skill performs no new research during the assessment.

evals.prompt: From the vault root, run /learn-quiz Caching. Both Learn/Operating Systems and Learn/Databases have an eligible topic named Caching.
evals.expected_output: Detects the cross-workspace ambiguity, asks the learner to select one workspace, and writes no assessment or state change before disambiguation.
assertions: The skill reads immediate Learn workspace progress files and detects both eligible matches.
The response names both workspaces and asks the learner to choose one.
No assessment artifact is created before disambiguation.
No progress row, date, Current Focus, or history entry changes.
The skill never combines topics from different workspaces into one assessment.

evals.prompt: Resume finalization of a complete-evidence Processes assessment whose intended progress change has already been applied but whose history event and Status complete write were interrupted.
evals.expected_output: Detects the already-applied transition, appends only the missing linked history event, marks the artifact complete, and leaves every existing progress field unchanged.
assertions: The skill recognizes finalization state from the assessment's intended progress changes.
The already-applied progress transition and Last Tested value are not rewritten or duplicated.
Exactly one missing history event is appended using the assessment link as the idempotency key.
The artifact is marked complete only after progress and history agree with its outcomes.
A second resume would make no further workspace changes.

evals.prompt: Run /learn-quiz with no arguments in Learn/Operating Systems, where Processes, Threads, and Context Switch are Needs Validation and Scheduling is Unexplored.
evals.expected_output: Lists only the three Needs Validation candidates, recommends a focused selection, asks the learner to confirm or exclude topics, and writes nothing before confirmation.
assertions: The response lists Processes, Threads, and Context Switch as candidates and does not list Scheduling as eligible.
The response asks the learner to confirm or exclude candidates and recommends a focused one-to-three-topic assessment.
No assessment artifact is created before topic confirmation.
No progress row, date, Current Focus, or history entry changes.
The skill does not begin a lesson or ask the first assessment question before confirmation.

evals.prompt: Start /learn-quiz Processes Threads, answer both Processes questions, then interrupt immediately after the first Threads prompt is persisted.
evals.expected_output: Leaves one in-progress artifact with complete Processes evidence and the unanswered Threads prompt while preserving all progress and history until the full batch can finalize.
assertions: The first prompt existed in the turn snapshot before the learner's first answer.
Processes has durable recall, transfer, and a topic outcome in the in-progress artifact.
Threads has a persisted unanswered prompt rather than a regenerated or pre-answered question.
Every selected progress row, date, Current Focus, and history entry remains identical to the initial vault.
The artifact remains in-progress and no completion history event exists.

evals.prompt: During /learn-quiz Context Switch, dispute corrective feedback and require resolution only from persisted workspace sources, which do not settle the claim.
evals.expected_output: Persists the dispute and unresolved resolution, leaves the assessment in-progress, and changes no progress or completion history while performing no research.
assertions: The learner's dispute is persisted in the assessment artifact.
Resolution records that persisted sources do not settle the grading question.
The assessment remains in-progress and has no final topic outcome or Progress Changes.
Progress and history remain byte-preserved.
No research or new source is introduced during the assessment.

evals.prompt: Resume a Processes finalization whose artifact baseline says Needs Validation but whose progress row now contains a conflicting human edit.
evals.expected_output: Detects the baseline conflict before applying or completing anything, reports it, and preserves the entire vault unchanged.
assertions: In-progress recovery is selected before new-attempt eligibility despite the current row status.
The current row matches neither the recorded baseline nor intended result, so finalization stops as a conflict.
No assessment field, progress field, history event, lesson, note, mission, map, or resource changes.
The artifact remains in-progress.
The response identifies the concurrent-edit conflict and asks the learner to reconcile it outside finalization.
